findings.evidence: Table 7-1, row "Total parameters": "70B | canonical 70B full-MHA teaching model [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]" — wait, the actual row reads: "Total parameters | 70B | [canonical scenario][DERIVED from 70B × 2 bytes]" — verbatim from p.125 Table 7-1: '70B | canonical 70B full-MHA teaching model [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]' for the layers row, but for 'Total parameters' the derivation cell reads '[canonical scenario][DERIVED from 70B × 2 bytes]'. Checking the provenance convention stated in Note 1 (Table 4-2, p.74): 'an input or parameter assumption (traffic, latency target, price, token count) is [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]'. 70B total parameters is a canonical-scenario input, not an arithmetic derivation. Table 4-2 (p.70) correctly tags 'Model parameters 70B' as '[canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]'. Table 7-1 mis-tags the same value as [DERIVED].
findings.issue: Table 7-1 (p.125) tags 'Total parameters 70B' as [canonical scenario][DERIVED], contradicting the book's own labeling convention that canonical-scenario input parameters are [ASSUMPTION]. Table 4-2 (p.70) correctly tags the same 70B value as [ASSUMPTION]. A locally wrong label on a foundational quantity propagates confusion when other chapters re-cite the table.
findings.fix_instruction: Change the epistemic-status tag on the 'Total parameters' row in Table 7-1 from [DERIVED] to [ASSUMPTION], matching Table 4-2 p.70 and Note 1's rule that input/parameter assumptions are [ASSUMPTION]. Keep the 'from 70B × 2 bytes' note on the FP16 residency row (which is genuinely derived) but separate it from the parameter-count row.

findings.evidence: p.144: 'The contrast between these two floors — inference ~164.1 GB for a 70B model at FP16 with 9.2K input (140 + 24.1; the 9.5K-max is 164.9 ≈ 165 GB) [canonical scenario][DERIVED], fine-tuning exceeding 1 TB [canonical scenario][DERIVED]'. Then p.149: 'the ~500 GB headroom (Ch. 4/7, single-request) and the ~436 GB KV budget (Ch. 17, concurrency) answer different questions'. The ~500 GB is 640 − 140 = 500 (weights subtracted from pool, KV not yet subtracted). The ~436 GB is 640 − 140 − 64 = 436 (weights and runtime reserve subtracted). Both are labeled 'headroom' or 'budget' in the same paragraph without the ~64 GB runtime reserve being mentioned as the differentiating term. The sentence 'the ~500 GB headroom ... and the ~436 GB KV budget ... answer different questions' does not state that the 64 GB difference IS the runtime reserve — a reader must cross-reference §7.1 (p.144) to understand why the two numbers differ by 64 GB.
findings.issue: Two different 'headroom/budget' figures (~500 GB and ~436 GB) are cited side by side on p.149 without stating that the 64 GB difference is the runtime/workspace reserve. The text says they 'answer different questions' but does not name the arithmetic that separates them (500 = 640−140; 436 = 640−140−64). A reader encountering only p.149 cannot reconcile the two numbers without jumping to §7.1.
findings.fix_instruction: On p.149, after 'answer different questions', add the one-clause reconciliation: '(~500 GB = 640 − 140 weights, before the ~64 GB runtime reserve; ~436 GB = 640 − 140 − 64, after it)'. This makes the two figures self-explanatory at the point of use.

findings.evidence: p.145, §7.7, third bullet: '(a) decode-time KV offload to CPU DRAM trades TPOT/ITL and KV capacity, not TTFT (TTFT is already complete when decode starts); (b) prefix/KV reuse loaded from CPU can reduce TTFT for cache-hit requests — the vLLM KV Offloading Connector's 2–22× figure is defined in Ch 6 (TTFT metric, warm-cache-hit/reuse benchmark) [S7][1P][FACT] and is highly prompt-size-dependent.' The label [S7][1P][FACT] is attached to a compound sentence that includes both (i) a definitional cross-reference (which TTFT metric is used) and (ii) a factual claim (the 2–22× figure exists and is warm-cache-specific). The label applies to the factual part but sits after a semicolon within a sentence whose first clause ('is defined in Ch 6') is a cross-reference, not a fact. Also, the p.118 §6.6 version states 'cuts TTFT by 2–22× in a particular warm-cache-hit/reuse benchmark, not a generic cold-cache improvement — both are memory-layer fixes' — the p.145 version adds 'highly prompt-size-dependent' which is NOT in the p.118 version and carries no separate label.
findings.issue: The [S7][1P][FACT] label on p.145 covers a sentence that mixes a cross-reference, a factual figure, and an unlabeled interpretive qualifier ('highly prompt-size-dependent'). The interpretive qualifier appears only on p.145 and has no provenance label — it is the book's own interpretation of the source, not a first-party fact. Meanwhile the p.118 version of the same claim omits this qualifier entirely, creating two slightly different restatements of the same source claim.
findings.fix_instruction: Split the sentence: (1) keep [S7][1P][FACT] on 'the vLLM KV Offloading Connector's 2–22× figure ... warm-cache-hit/reuse benchmark'; (2) tag 'highly prompt-size-dependent' as [DERIVED] or [HYPOTHESIS] (it is the book's inference from the benchmark description); (3) either add the same qualifier to p.118 or remove it from p.145 for consistency.

findings.chapter: Ch 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint
findings.evidence: Fig 7.7 in-figure text: 'Concurrency budget — one 8×H100 host / 140 GB weights / ~64 GB runtime/NCCL / ~436 GB KV budget / 640 GB pool / in-flight ≈ KV budget ÷ KV per request / ≈ 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB ≈ 17.5 → ~17 requests'. Caption: "Naming note: the arithmetic panel reads 'in-flight'; that quantity is the KV-resident slot count (concurrent sequences holding a KV slot), not the Little's-Law in-flight request count."
findings.issue: Figure-vs-caption contradiction, same defect family as FR-001/XR-005 but a distinct artifact. The caption concedes that the figure's own label is the wrong term and issues a naming note instead of correcting the figure. Since the book uses 'in-flight' throughout for the Little's-Law quantity (e.g. p. 85: 'the in-flight concurrency λ·W ≈ 344'; p. 100: '344 in flight'), leaving 'in-flight' inside a figure that means something else — and doing so with an in-caption erratum — is an active trap for a reader who consults figures rather than captions. The List of Figures entry (p. 10) reads 'The concurrency budget' with no indication that the figure's headline label uses a term the book elsewhere reserves for a different quantity.
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the Fig 7.7 panel to 'KV-resident slots ≈ KV budget ÷ KV per request' and delete the caption's naming note (or reduce it to a one-line pointer). Add 'KV-resident slots' as the term used in all body references so the figure, caption, §7.3, §4.6 and Ch 17 agree.

findings.chapter: Ch 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint
findings.evidence: Fig 7.8 in-figure labels: 'Memory Tetris: how the 8×H100 host (640 GB) fills with context', 'KV cache (grows with context)', 'weights 140 GB', 'runtime / NCCL ~64 GB', 'KV 24.9 GB', '9.5K context = 229 GB used', 'KV 84 GB', '32K context = 288 GB used', 'KV 335 GB', '128K context = 539 GB used', '640 GB = 8× 80 GB ranks (light rules = 80 GB rank boundaries)'. Caption: "The totals are 228.9 GB at 9.5K (shown as 229), 287.9 GB at 32K (shown as 288) and 539.5 GB at 128K (the figure’s scale label reads 539); that 0.5 GB is a label-rounding artifact against a 640 GB axis, not a capacity claim."
findings.issue: Figure-vs-caption numeric-label divergence left in the artifact and excused in the caption. The figure's scale label reads 539 GB while the underlying total is 539.5 GB; the caption explains this away but the figure is the artifact a reader consults. The same figure also labels the 32K KV block as 'KV 84 GB' while the book's own body figure for 32K is 83.9 GB (Table 7-1, p. 126: '32K input KV cache … 83.9 GB'; and Fig 7.5's caption on p. 147: 'at 128K the FP16 KV footprint is ~335 GB'), and the 128K block as 'KV 335 GB' where Table 7-1 says 335.5 GB. Two different rounding conventions ('84' vs '83.9', '335' vs '335.5', '539' vs '539.5') coexist inside one figure with the caption calling out only the last. Per the recurrence rule this rounding-drift family also appears on p. 146 ('KV cache per token (FP16) … ≈ 2.62 MB' with the exact 2,621,440 B given elsewhere) and on p. 147's '83.9 GB'/'335.5 GB' versus Fig 7.5's axis text.
findings.fix_instruction: Adopt one rounding rule for the whole chapter (the chapter states it on p. 145: 'per-request KV is quoted as 24.9 GB (byte-accurate 24.90368 GB)'), apply it to every in-figure label (84 → 83.9, 335 → 335.5, 539 → 539.5), and remove the caption's rounding-apology paragraph. Then reconcile Table 7-1, Fig 7.5's axis text and Fig 7.8 to the same rule.

findings.chapter: Ch 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint
findings.evidence: Fig 7.2 in-figure text: 'Hybrid history: two state lifetimes', 'Schematic token snapshots; not a performance comparison', 'token t1 / recurrent update / state after t1 fixed-size state / KV1 / 1 cached token', 'token t2 … KV1 KV2 / 2 cached tokens', 'token t3 … KV1 KV2 KV3 / 3 cached tokens', 'Successive state snapshots, not jointly retained history', 'Full-attention layers: growing key/value (KV) history', 'Recurrent updates compute; state and KV boxes store', 'Arrows = token input / state flow; snapshots are schematic'. Caption: "Configuration-backed example (Qwen3.8-27B), not a measured memory ratio."
findings.issue: Figure-vs-caption scope mismatch: the caption asserts the figure is a 'Configuration-backed example (Qwen3.8-27B)', but the figure itself carries no configuration values at all — no layer counts, no KV-head count, no head dimension, no byte totals. A reader cannot tell which part of the figure is Qwen3.8-27B-specific (the 16 full-attention layers and 48 Gated DeltaNet layers are given only in the body text on p. 153, '16 full-attention layers, four KV-heads per layer, and a head dimension of 256'), so the figure as drawn is a generic schematic, not a configuration-backed example. The List of Figures entry (p. 9) reads 'History recurrence and attention history have different lifetimes' with no configuration qualifier, so the only place the Qwen attribution appears is the caption — and the figure does not bear it out.
findings.fix_instruction: Either annotate Fig 7.2 with the configuration numbers it claims to be backed by (16 full-attention layers, 4 KV heads, head dim 256, BF16 → 65,536 B/token; 48 recurrent layers) or change the caption to 'Schematic of a hybrid-attention history budget; the configuration-backed instance (Qwen3.8-27B) is worked in the text' so the artifact and the caption agree. Apply the same test to Figs 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3, whose captions likewise claim configuration or first-party backing.

findings.chapter: Ch 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint
findings.evidence: p. 144 (Ch 7 §7.1): "The residency floor has two distinct regimes. For inference, the floor is weights + KV: … inference ~164.1 GB for a 70B model at FP16 with 9.2K input (140 + 24.1; the 9.5K-max is 164.9 ≈ 165 GB) … fine-tuning exceeding 1 TB". p. 146 (Table 7-1): "inference residency (weights + KV, 9.5K max) ≈ 165 GB — 140 + 24.9 GB"; 'fits 8×H100 at 9.2K? yes — 164.1 GB < 640 GB'. p. 148 (Fig 7.6 in-figure): '~165 GB'. p. 163 (Ch 7 §7.6): "the max end-of-generation residency ≈ 165 GB". p. 28 (Ch 1 §1.1.5): "At 9.2K tokens the canonical FP16 KV per request is ~24.1 GB … 9,200 × 2,621,440 B = 24,117,248,000 B ≈ 24.12 GB". p. 163: "FP8 KV ≈ 50% of FP16 … dropping the 9.5K max residency from ~165 GB toward ~152 GB". p. 155 (Table 7-2): "inference with FP8 KV … ~152 GB (9.5K; 140 + 12.45; KV alone 12.45 GB)".
findings.issue: Definitional drift in the KV-per-request basis, and a decimal/rounding inconsistency in the same quantity across chapters. Ch 1 states the canonical 9.2K KV as '~24.1 GB' with the exact figure '≈ 24.12 GB'; Ch 7 Table 7-1 states '9,200 ×2.62 MB ≈ 24.1 GB' and the 9.5K basis as '≈ 24.9 GB' (exact 24.90368 GB, stated in the p. 145 rounding rule). Ch 3 Table 3-3 uses '~24.1 GB' at 9.2K and '~12.06 GB' at 8-bit. Ch 5 Table 5-2 uses '~24.1 GB (FP16 KV cache, initial)'. So 24.1 GB (Ch 1's 24.12) and 24.9 GB (Ch 7's 24.90) are both live 'canonical' values for the same quantity at the same context, differing by the input-only vs input+output basis — which Ch 4 Table 4-2 does document ('~24.1 GB @ 9.2K input-only; ~24.9 GB @ 9.5K input+output — the resident slot-counting basis, §4.6'), so the basis is defined once but the Ch 1 and Ch 5 usages do not carry it. Separately, the FP8 9.5K KV figure is '12.06 GB' in Chs 1 and 3 (at the 9.2K input basis) but '12.45 GB' in Ch 7 Table 7-2 and §7.6 (at the 9.5K resident basis) — and p. 28 (Ch 1) explicitly warns against the FP8 figure being quoted at the wrong basis ('the 8-bit variant is not ~13.4 GB'), which shows the book knows the basis matters. A reader comparing '~12.06 GB' (Ch 1/3) with '~12.45 GB' (Ch 7) sees an unexplained 3% discrepancy for the same named quantity ('FP8 KV for the canonical request').
findings.fix_instruction: State the basis inside every quoted KV-per-request figure (e.g. '24.1 GB @ 9.2K input-only' / '24.9 GB @ 9.5K resident'), and reconcile the FP8 pair explicitly: add a line to Table 7-1 giving the FP8 9.2K figure as 12.06 GB alongside the 9.5K figure as 12.45 GB, so Chs 1, 3, 5 and 7 all quote both bases for both precisions. Apply the same to the residency totals: '164.1 GB @ 9.2K' vs '165 GB @ 9.5K' should always carry the basis.

findings.chapter: Ch 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint
findings.evidence: p. 145 (Ch 7 §7.3): "Rounding rule for this section: per-request KV is quoted as 24.9 GB (byte-accurate 24.90368 GB); every quotient below is computed on the byte-accurate value and then floored to whole slots, and the FP8 figure of 12.45 GB is the raw byte-halving of that same value (12.45184 GB)." Compare p. 143 (Ch 7 §7.1): "the ~64 GB is a planning reserve, not a measured constant." Compare p. 149 (Fig 7.7 caption): '436 GB KV budget'; p. 168 (Fig 7.5 caption): 'the ~436 GB KV budget = 640 GB aggregate pool − 140 GB weights − 64 GB runtime/workspace'.
findings.issue: Rounding-rule scope conflict and an undeclared denominator for the KV budget. Ch 7 §7.3 declares a section-scoped rounding rule ('per-request KV is quoted as 24.9 GB … every quotient below is computed on the byte-accurate value'), but the same chapter's §7.1 (p. 143) and §7.2–7.3 elsewhere quote 24.1 GB at 9.2K, and Chs 1, 3 and 5 quote the same quantity as '~24.1 GB' with the exact byte count given as 24,117,248,000 B ≈ 24.12 GB — a third value for the same quantity. Separately, the '436 GB KV budget' is used as the denominator for the concurrency screen (436 ÷ 24.90368 = 17.51 → 17) but is itself a rounded figure: 640 − 140 − 64 = 436 exactly, so the budget is exact while the per-request value is not, and the chapter's §7.1 explicitly makes the 64 GB reserve an [ASSUMPTION] that 'must come from a deployment benchmark' — meaning the 17-slot ceiling inherits an unmeasured denominator without a sensitivity note. By contrast p. 143's unit-basis note says the vendor-binary reading would give '~480 GB' and '~19' slots, so the book knows the denominator is convention-dependent but the canonical figures do not carry the caveat into the tables that consume them.
findings.fix_instruction: Promote the rounding rule from §7.3 to the chapter intro (or the Preface's conventions) and apply it book-wide; state the KV budget as '436 GB (640 − 140 − 64, where the 64 GB runtime reserve is an [ASSUMPTION])' in every table/figure that consumes it, and add a one-line sensitivity (vendor-binary basis: 480 GB → 19 slots) to Table 7-1 or Fig 7.7 so the denominator's convention-dependence travels with the number.

findings.evidence: Fig 7.8 caption: "consuming the fixed ~436 GB KV budget (~17.5 → 17 concurrent at 9.5K; 436 ÷ 83.9 = 5.2 → 5 at 32K; 436 ÷ 335.46 = 1.30 → 1 at 128K)". Table 7-1 (PDF 146): "128,000 ×2,621,440 B ≈ 335.5 GB"; the same caption states "539.5 GB at 128K" (= 140 + 64 + 335.5).
findings.issue: Divisor slip: the book's own 128K per-request KV figure is 335.5 GB (exact: 128,000 × 2,621,440 B = 335,544,320,000 B = 335.54 GB); '335.46' matches neither the exact constant (2.62144 MB) nor the printed constant (2.62 MB → 335.36). The quotient 1.30 is unaffected (436 ÷ 335.54 = 1.299), so this is a caption typo, not a computational error.
findings.fix_instruction: Change '335.46' to '335.5' (or 335.54) in the Fig 7.8 caption so it agrees with Table 7-1, Fig 7.5 and the caption's own 539.5 GB total.

findings.evidence: Fig 7.5 caption (PDF 167): "FP8 shown as raw tensor byte-halving (exactly 50% of BF16, ~1.31 MB/tok)". §7.4 (PDF 162): "State both the BF16 and FP8 residency numbers, because the choice of KV dtype changes the hardware requirement decisively." Counterparts: Ch 7 intro (PDF 142): "the canonical scenario's KV constant is the FP16 2.62 MB/token figure"; §7.6 (PDF 163): "FP8 KV ≈ 50% of FP16 (raw byte-halving)"; Table 7-1 (PDF 146): "exactly 50% of the 16-bit (FP16/BF16) baseline"; Table 4-2: "KV precision FP16".
findings.issue: Baseline-label drift for the same constant: the canonical KV baseline is FP16, but Fig 7.5's caption names BF16 as the 50% reference and §7.4 says 'the BF16 and FP8 residency numbers'. Bytes are identical (both 2-byte), so no number changes, but the chapter's own intro/§7.6/Table 4-2 fix the label as FP16, and Ch 2 §2.5 stresses that load-bearing contrasts are never relaxed.
findings.fix_instruction: Standardize the KV-baseline label in Fig 7.5's caption and §7.4 to FP16 (or use Table 7-1's dual form '16-bit (FP16/BF16)') so all Ch 7 references to the 2.62 MB/token baseline use one name.
